title: Drought-flood alternation under climate change
description: Climate change is increasing the frequency of both droughts and floods, meaning back-to-back extreme events are also on the rise. These rapidly alternating crises can harm people in complex ways. For example, back-to-back climate extremes can stress crops, reducing yields.

title: Mitotic chromosomes may assemble from pre-existing chromatin 'building blocks' during cell division
description: Inside each human cell, about 2 meters (6.6 feet) of genomic DNA must be accurately copied and equally transmitted to two daughter cells during cell division. To achieve this, the copied DNA is condensed into thick, short structures called mitotic chromosomes. However, how chromatin is organized and condensed to form mitotic chromosomes has long remained a major question in genetics and cell biol…

title: Is science journalism dying? Comparing a 'science crash' 40 years ago to today
description: When two popular science magazines—out of about 17 in circulation—ceased publication in the same year, one commentator said, "The science magazines didn't shake out. They fell apart." The general manager of one of the failed magazines said, "There was a perception that they were irrelevant." One of the publishers remembered being in a "state of shock" as the failures emerged.

title: Record-breaking levels of plastic found in seabirds, with almost 900 pieces found in one bird alone
description: For more than a decade, it was thought that the world's most plastic-polluted birds couldn't get any more contaminated by the man-made material. But then, from 2023–2026, the record was broken every single year.

title: 3D food printing of balanced vegetarian dishes from rice and lentil flours
description: Rice and lentils are a pairing that goes a long way back, whether as khichdi in India or mujaddara in the Middle East. On its own, each is a source of incomplete protein, short on certain essential amino acids—but paired together, they fill each other's gaps, and lentils also blunt white rice's high glycemic index.

title: Greenhouse gas benefits of agricultural irrigation far outweigh emissions costs, study finds
description: Irrigating U.S. crops prevents higher greenhouse gas emissions by avoiding land conversion, new research by Colorado State University shows. Agricultural irrigation allows the United States to grow more food on less land. If irrigation were suddenly shut off, the land-use change required to make up for lost yields would produce significantly more greenhouse gas emissions than irrigation emits—363…

title: Heat-stable enzyme from deep-sea microbe turns nitrogen gas into ammonia
description: Microorganisms can do remarkable things—for example, nitrogen fixation, the conversion of nitrogen gas (N₂) into a form that organisms can use. Although nitrogen gas makes up around 78% of Earth's atmosphere, plants and animals cannot directly use it.

title: How advertising turns our insecurities into profit—and how you can resist the manipulation
description: Have you ever bought something not because you wanted it, but because you were afraid of what might happen if you didn't? Maybe you worried about looking older, falling behind at work or simply not fitting in.

title: Wild dogs make the longest recorded journey of any terrestrial mammal in Africa
description: African wild dogs (Lycaon pictus) travel incredibly long distances to search for a mate and new places to breed. They typically embark on these mammoth treks as young adults and often face numerous hazards along the way. These include busy highways, expanding human settlements and deadly wire poaching snares.

title: Avoiding a sticky situation: How cells stop messenger RNAs from clumping together
description: Messenger RNA, or mRNA, is best known for carrying genetic instructions from DNA to the cellular machinery that makes proteins. But all RNA molecules have another, less appreciated property: They are naturally sticky.

title: Frontline safety concerns mount among property managers, new survey shows
description: Safety and security challenges are creating unprecedented strain for frontline property management professionals, according to a new bilingual survey conducted by Portland State University's Center for Real Estate. Initiated after industry partners raised alarms about changing workplace conditions, the study offers insight into the daily risks experienced by property management staff at multifami…

title: CubeSat instrument extends solar storm warnings 10x
description: The sun is the reason life exists on our small, blue planet. It provides solar radiation that warms the planet and ignites intricate biochemical processes like photosynthesis, producing oxygen for life to breathe. However, while the sun is known for giving life, it can also take it away with solar flares, geomagnetic storms and solar radiation storms, collectively referred to as space weather.

title: Satellite data reveal ESG scores track public image more than actual forest loss
description: Environmental sustainability researchers at NUS found that widely used environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings often fail to reflect companies' actual exposure to deforestation, highlighting the need to integrate satellite-based environmental data into sustainable investing frameworks.

title: How individual cells 'surf' chemical waves to form a collective
description: Researchers have developed an innovative imaging technique to visualize the transition of single cells into multicellular organisms in new detail.

title: Biophysical model suggests how cells optimize information gathering without using too much energy
description: In both biological and engineered systems, cells and sensors must make sense of noisy, changing signals to function. However, collecting and using this information consumes valuable energy. A new study, published in Physical Review Letters, describes a model for how a sensor or cell might maximize information collection from its surroundings while controlling the overall energy cost, resulting in…

title: Local experience shapes how coastal communities understand and respond to climate change
description: While people across the globe are experiencing various impacts of climate change, governments and communicators often use top-to-bottom, uniform communication strategies to inform people about climate change.

title: Fertilizer study reveals where the world can boost food production and cut pollution
description: Global consumption of fertilizer has doubled since 1980, but some regions that have historically overused fertilizer, including China and parts of Europe, have taken steps to reduce use. Those are some of the findings of a new global dataset from the University of Minnesota's Institute on the Environment.

title: New research calls for more consistent, child-centered policing to build trust and protect children
description: New research co-led by the University of Bedfordshire and the University of Lancashire has highlighted the need for more consistent child-centered and safeguarding-led approaches across policing, with children and young people's experiences varying depending on where they live, whom they encounter, the reason for these encounters and how well systems support frontline practice.

title: Examining Americans' complicated relationship with science
description: A new study finds that while most Americans are interested in science and believe it benefits society, the public's relationship with science is more complicated than those positive views suggest.

title: Planting trees in the wrong places is not a climate solution
description: A recent United Nations report has stated that the world will likely overshoot the 1.5°C target set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement by 2030.

title: Marine bacteria team up to break down one of the ocean's toughest carbon-storing molecules
description: Deep in the ocean, brown algae and diatoms produce a complex carbohydrate molecule called fucoidan, which helps form their protective outer layers. The fucoidan molecule is very difficult for microbes to break down because its chemical structure may include dozens of different linkages and branching patterns that vary from one algal species to another.

title: Scientists create 'super ice' that is ten times stronger and far harder to shatter
description: Ice is cheap, abundant and surprisingly strong. But it has one major weakness: Cracks can race through it, causing it to shatter without warning. Now, scientists have developed a new material that could overcome that problem. Called BioPykrete, the reinforced ice is about 10 times stronger than ordinary ice and can absorb roughly 70 times more energy before breaking.

title: Advanced X-ray crystallography determines structure of macromolecule at unprecedented resolution
description: Proteins are high-performance molecular machines that carry out nearly every biochemical function inside living cells. To understand how they achieve this, scientists often examine their detailed atomic structure, which holds important clues to their activity. The more precision they achieve, the deeper the insight they may gain into the chemical principles that underlie protein structure and, ul…

title: Ancient DNA traces medieval migration from Sweden to Finland
description: A new study led by the University of Turku provides new insights into the population history of Finland during the Late Iron Age and the Middle Ages. The researchers analyzed the genomes of people who lived in southwestern Finland and Häme between the 11th and 13th centuries to investigate how the population changed over the course of the Middle Ages and how people were connected to other regions…

title: Europe's e‑waste is a valuable resource—let's not throw it away
description: Throwing something away that is urgently needed, expensive and difficult to source sounds crazy. Yet of the 60 metals contained in old electronic devices such as phones, screens and washing machines, only a few are recycled. That includes precious metals such as gold and silver and other metals such as aluminum and copper. The rest are effectively single-use metals, used once and then lost during…

title: Our new research shows humans have maligned bandicoots for decades, making them more vulnerable to extinction
description: Have you ever found your lawn riddled with holes or heard a little sneeze from your backyard bushes? Those are signs you might have a resident bandicoot. Bandicoots are nocturnal, rabbit-sized marsupials known for their pointy snouts, thin tails and large hind feet. Due to these features, they were originally misnamed after a type of rat from India, the pandi-kokku, or "pig-rat" (Bandicota sp.).

title: Laser altimeter BELA ready to explore Mercury's surface
description: Launched on Oct. 20, 2018, the joint ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission has traveled for almost eight years, using a carefully planned but eventful sequence of planetary flybys and solar-electric propulsion to gradually approach its destination, Mercury. The mission is now entering the final stage of its journey to the smallest and innermost planet of our solar system.

title: 68% of physicists don’t think the time started at the big bang
description: A recent survey shows researchers remain divided on fundamental concepts. But that’s not a bad thing. The post 68% of physicists don’t think the time started at the big bang appeared first on Popular Science .

title: It’s almost time to airdrop rabies vaccines again
description: The USDA program uses fishmeal-coated bait bricks to lure raccoons and other animals. The post It’s almost time to airdrop rabies vaccines again appeared first on Popular Science .

title: ‘What Is Missing?’: Stunning exhibition by Maya Lin opens new gallery at Briger Hall
description: The centerpiece of the exhibition is a two-story multimedia display that presents immersive, larger-than-life audio and video of threatened and endangered species. The show opens with an artist talk Sept. 22.

title: Israeli Airstrikes Pound Gaza, Kill One and Injure Others as Death Toll Rises
description: Gaza, September 15 (QNA) - The Gaza Strip has been coming under unabated firepower launched by Israeli occupation combat aircraft since dawn Tuesday, killing a Palestinian and wounding others, some of whom are in critical condition, Palestinian medical sources reported.

title: UAE, Syria Presidents Discuss Middle East Developments, Regional Stability
description: Abu Dhabi, September 15 (QNA) - HH President of the United Arab Emirates Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan met Tuesday with President Ahmed Al Sharaa of Syria during his visit to the UAE.

title: Israeli Attacks on Southern Lebanon Continue
description: Beirut, September 15 (QNA) - Israeli forces continued their attacks on towns in southern Lebanon today, carrying out artillery shelling and machine-gun fire.

title: Oman's Foreign Minister, US Secretary of State Discuss Regional Developments
description: Muscat, September 15 (QNA) - Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi spoke Tuesday with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss the recent developments unfolding in the region.

title: Kuwaiti Foreign Minister, UK National Security Advisor Discuss Regional Developments
description: London, September 15 (QNA) - Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, currently visiting London, discussed the latest regional developments with British National Security Advisor Jonathan Powell.

title: Egyptian President, Saudi Crown Prince Discuss Regional Developments
description: Cairo, September 15 (QNA) - Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El Sisi and HH Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud discussed regional developments during His Highness' current visit to Cairo.

title: Canada's Carney seeking closer EU ties, to attend State of the EU address
description: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney will become the first non-EU head of government to attend the State of the Union address as he seeks to bring Canada and the EU closer in the face of a hostile United States.

title: Workers across France stage protests over pay and rising costs
description: Protests are taking place across France on Tuesday, with fishermen, police officers, energy workers, university staff and other groups mobilising over a range of demands. Better pay, working conditions and the high cost of energy are among the main concerns.

title: Environmental activists angry over controversial AI data centre near Paris
description: France is preparing to build Europe’s largest artificial intelligence data centre in a village outside of Paris. The government hopes to boost its computing infrastructure and give France an edge in the global race to develop AI, but activists are concerned about the impacts on health and the environment.

title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania in latest Baltic security incident
description: NATO fighter jets shot have down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security incident on Europe's border with Russia as its war with Ukraine continues.

title: International justice 'can't be erased' despite US sanctions: ICC prosecutor
description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is facing US sanctions since deciding to issue arrest warrants over alleged war crimes in Gaza. Mame Mandiaye Niang, the Senegalese magistrate who has been acting head of the ICC's Office of the Prosecutor since his predecessor Karim Khan was forced out, tells RFI that while the Court's resilience is being tested, its existence is not under threat.

title: Finland joins French nuclear umbrella amid European security push
description: Finland has decided to join France’s nuclear deterrence umbrella in a bid to bolster regional security in the face of uncertainty over the United States' commitment to Europe and NATO.

title: France says Russia seeks to 'intimidate' EU with train attack near Poland
description: France and the European Union have condemned a Russian strike on a passenger train on the Polish border that has raised concerns about the risks of the war spreading closer to EU and NATO territory.

title: France seeks EU backing for revised social media ban for under-15s
description: A month after France’s Constitutional Council struck down a proposed social media ban for under-15s, the government has submitted a new version that President Emmanuel Macron wants passed before he leaves office in the spring.

title: World in Frames: RFI traces the stories behind the world's most famous photos
description: As France marks 200 years since inventor Nicéphore Niépce took the world’s oldest surviving photograph, RFI looks back at photos that changed our view of history – or even history itself. Here we tell the story of how a portrait of an unnamed woman came to represent the suffering of a nation in Dorothea Lange’s Migrant Mother, and what the iconic picture left out.

title: 'Historic day' for Nigeria as Dangote oil refinery launches IPO
description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa's biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion (€1.3 billion) to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world's largest.

title: Growing budgets show Africa keen to defend its place in the space race
description: African states invest around $500 million in space programmes annually, a figure expected to reach around $40 billion by 2030. With a number of initiatives already in place, the continent is seeking a seat at the table when it comes to international decisions on space exploration and equal access to the development of technology.

title: Normandy derailment inquiry widens focus on rail fragment found on track
description: A technical investigation has been launched into the derailment of a regional train near Rouen that left 44 people injured, as authorities work to establish how a piece of rail came to be lying on the track.

title: Sweden's election too close to call, left opposition narrowly leads
description: Sweden's general election is still too close to call, with Magdalena Andersson’s centre-left opposition coalition holding a narrow lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing alliance.

title: Macron, Carney to visit French Atlantic islands with sovereignty message to Trump
description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will visit the French North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon next week, in a symbolic show of support for national sovereignty amid renewed territorial claims by US President Donald Trump.

title: France moves to defuse US row over UN social media post
description: France has expressed regret over a social media post questioning the United States’ commitment to human rights, in a move expected to clear the way for its new ambassador to take up his post in Washington.

title: French Rafale jets take flight for 40,000-kilometre mission over three-continents
description: Four French Rafale fighter jets have embarked on a 40-day mission spanning three continents, highlighting France’s ability to deploy its air power around the world while strengthening cooperation with key international partners.

title: Radio France staff strike over appointment of right-wing magazine editor
description: Radio France staff began a two-day strike on Sunday over France Inter’s decision to hire a senior editor from the right-wing magazine Valeurs actuelles as a political commentator. Charles Sapin’s appointment has drawn criticism because the magazine has previously been convicted of racist public insult and incitement to racial hatred.

title: As catches dwindle, Congo River fishermen turn to plastic waste
description: On the Congo River, plastic is becoming the catch of the day. Some fishermen around Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, can now make more money pulling plastic from the water than catching fish, as declining catches and growing waste pollution threaten an artisanal way of life.

title: From townships to TikTok, South Africa's amapiano gets the world dancing
description: Amapiano dancers across South Africa are helping a sound born in the country's black townships reach audiences far beyond its borders – one viral challenge at a time. Short routines filmed in homes, schools and public spaces are spreading across social media, giving musicians another way to promote a genre that's now a global hit.

title: Erdogan hints at larger nuclear partnership with Russia, unsettling Turkey's allies
description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is signalling a move to expand nuclear power cooperation with Russia, just as his country’s first Russian-built nuclear station prepares to go live later this year. The deepening partnership is likely to unsettle Turkey’s western allies.

title: Before its peak, El Nino brings failed crops and empty fishing nets
description: El Nino is already disrupting livelihoods and weather patterns around the world as one of the strongest events in decades continues to intensify. With its peak still months away, scientists warn the powerful Pacific climate phenomenon will bring more drought and flooding into 2027, while human-caused global warming is making some of its effects more severe.

title: How 100 days of record ocean heat is reshaping life in and around the seas
description: Global oceans have endured 100 consecutive days of record average heat, as human-driven climate change pushes temperatures higher and puts growing pressure on marine life. Scientists say prolonged warming is disrupting fisheries, damaging coral reefs, raising sea levels and threatening economies that depend on healthy seas.

description: By most accounts, the Ukrainian counteroffensive is shaping up to be one of the largest shifts on the battlefield in months, possibly in a year.
